text: Modern user interfaces are complex composites, with elements originating from various sources, such as the operating system, apps, a web browser, or websites. We posit that security and privacy decisions can to some extent depend on users correctly identifying an element’s source, a concept we term “surface attribution.” Through two large-scale vignette-based surveys (N = 4, 400 and N = 3, 057), we present the first empirical measurement of this ability.
